parts.text: Two events $A$ and $B$ are such that $P(A) = 0.40$, $P(B) = 0.35$, and $P(A \cap B) = 0.14$. Determine, showing clear numerical evidence, whether events $A$ and $B$ are independent.
Two events $C$ and $D$ satisfy $P(D) = 0.60$, $P(C \cap D) = 0.18$, and $P(C) = 0.25$. By calculating $P(C \mid D)$, determine whether events $C$ and $D$ are independent.

Two events $X$ and $Y$ have probabilities $P(X) = 0.40$ and $P(Y) = 0.50$. It is given that $X$ and $Y$ are mutually exclusive. State the value of $P(X \cap Y)$ and determine whether $X$ and $Y$ are independent.

questions.title: Single Die Independence of Parity and Threshold

parts.text: A fair 6-sided die is rolled once. Let $E$ be the event that the score is even, and let $F$ be the event that the score is greater than 4. By calculating $P(E)$, $P(F)$, and $P(E \cap F)$ from the sample space, determine whether events $E$ and $F$ are independent.

questions.title: Unknown Parameter from the Addition Rule under Independence

parts.text: Events $A$ and $B$ are independent. Given that $P(A) = 0.60$ and $P(A \cup B) = 0.84$, find $P(B)$.

A group of 50 students were surveyed about studying French ($F$) and German ($G$). Exactly 10 study both, 15 study French only, 10 study German only, and 15 study neither language. Determine whether studying French and studying German are independent.

A cohort of 120 students in Year 10 and Year 11 choose between Chess and Robotics. Among 45 Year 10 students, 18 choose Chess. Among 75 Year 11 students, 30 choose Chess. Let $Y$ be the event that a randomly chosen student is in Year 10, and let $C$ be the event that the student chooses Chess. Find $P(Y)$, $P(C)$, and $P(Y \cap C)$.
Using your answers to part (a), determine whether the event that a student is in Year 10 is independent of the event that the student chooses Chess.
For two events $A$ and $B$, it is given that $P(A) = 0.70$ and $P(B) = 0.40$. Given that $A$ and $B$ are independent, find $P(A \cap B)$ and $P(A \cup B)$.

In a different scenario with the same marginal probabilities $P(A) = 0.70$ and $P(B) = 0.40$, it is found that $P(A \cup B) = 0.85$. Find the value of $P(A \cap B)$ and determine whether $A$ and $B$ are independent in this scenario.

questions.title: Two Dice: Score Threshold and Sum Independence

parts.text: A red fair 6-sided die and a blue fair 6-sided die are rolled. Let $A$ be the event that the score on the red die is greater than 4. Let $B$ be the event that the sum of the two scores is 7. Find $P(A)$ and $P(B)$.
Find $P(A \cap B)$ by listing the favorable ordered outcomes, and determine whether events $A$ and $B$ are independent.

questions.title: Two Dice: Product Score and Even Parity

parts.text: Two fair 6-sided dice are thrown. Let $M$ be the event that the product of the two scores is at least 15, and let $E$ be the event that both scores are even. Find $P(M)$ and $P(E)$.
By identifying all outcomes that belong to $M \cap E$, find $P(M \cap E)$ and determine whether events $M$ and $E$ are independent.

questions.title: Survey Table with Unknown Parameter and Commuter Independence

parts.text: A survey of 200 adults categorized them by commute method (Public transport $T$, Car $C$) and residential area (Urban $U$, Suburban $S$). Among the 100 urban residents, 70 use public transport and 30 drive cars. Among the 100 suburban residents, $k$ use public transport and $100 - k$ drive cars. Express $P(U)$, $P(T)$, and $P(U \cap T)$ in terms of $k$ where necessary.
Given that commute method and residential area are independent, determine the value of $k$ and calculate $P(C \mid S)$.

questions.title: Permutations and Independence of Letter Positions

parts.text: The five distinct letters A, B, C, D, E are arranged randomly in a line. State the total number of possible arrangements, and find $P(X)$, where $X$ is the event that letter A occupies either the first position or the fifth position.
Let $Y$ be the event that letters B and C are next to each other. Find $P(Y)$.
Find $P(X \cap Y)$ and determine whether events $X$ and $Y$ are independent.

Electronic modules undergo two electrical tests, $E_1$ and $E_2$. It is given that $P(E_1) = 0.80$, $P(E_2) = 0.75$, and $P(E_1 \cap E_2) = 0.60$. Determine whether events $E_1$ and $E_2$ are independent.
A module is classified as Grade A if it passes at least one of the two electrical tests ($E_1 \cup E_2$). Find the probability that a randomly chosen module is classified as Grade A.

Each module also undergoes an optical visual inspection $V$, where $P(V) = 0.90$. The visual inspection is independent of the electrical tests. A module is Certified if it is Grade A and passes visual inspection. Find the probability that a module is Certified, and find the conditional probability that a Certified module passed both electrical tests $E_1$ and $E_2$.
